event_description: Statewide state of emergency for the Blizzard of 1978, declared at 9:15 p.m. on Monday, February 6, 1978, closing all roads to vehicles not engaged in cleanup or emergency work (Today in Connecticut History: "At 9:15pm, she declared a state of emergency").

State of emergency for the June 1982 floods, declared Monday, June 7, 1982, when the Governor also announced he would seek federal assistance (chronology in Realizing the Risk: A History of the June 1982 Floods in Connecticut, Department of Environmental Protection, 1983).

State of civil preparedness emergency after the July 10, 1989 tornadoes and severe storms in Hamden, Waterbury and Bantam, declared Tuesday, July 11, 1989 after the Governor toured the damage (Hartford Courant, July 12, 1989: "Gov. William A. O'Neill declared a state of emergency Tuesday").
State of emergency put in place after the March 13 to 14, 2010 nor'easter and still in force during the late March flooding (dated report of March 30, 2010; the signing day is not given).
Statewide civil preparedness emergency for a major snowstorm
Statewide state of emergency to obtain road salt for towns during repeated winter storms
Statewide civil preparedness emergency for Tropical Storm Henri
Executive Order 24-1: emergency actions for severe weather and flooding on the Yantic River, requiring emergency work at the Fitchville Pond Dam in Bozrah
Statewide state of emergency for critical fire weather, drought and multiple brush fires
Statewide state of emergency for a major winter storm
Statewide state of emergency for a blizzard
